title: Client-side metering offsets during propagation lag causing underreporting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers reported that their daily usage totals were ~3-7% lower than expected for the time window 2026-03-07T02:00Z -> 2026-03-08T08:00Z. Discrepancy appears across Hosted and Dedicated modes and for a small number of Private installs running older agent versions. Initial triage shows token ingest events were generated by our front-line SDKs, but the server-side metering pipeline did not persist a subset of short-lived requests when propagation lag between the ingestion tier and the aggregation tier exceeded the SDK's request TTL.

Scope & impact: Affected customers: 7 paying customers (2 Hosted, 3 Dedicated, 2 Private) with heavy short-interaction patterns (many 1-3 token responses). Estimated revenue exposure: underbilling by ~3-7% for the window; immediate customer complaints about 'missing usage' and invoice reconciliation mismatches. No data loss in model outputs; this is strictly accounting/metering.

Root cause hypothesis: The SDK sends a lightweight metering envelope alongside each request which contains a short-lived client timestamp and routing tag. When ingestion tier experienced a transient propagation lag (up to 90s) due to a control-plane traffic spike, the ingestion node applied an eviction policy for envelopes older than 30s to reduce memory pressure. A race condition in the ingestion -> aggregator handoff meant that envelopes marked as "expired" were dropped rather than forwarded to the long-term aggregator, but the corresponding token charges were already removed from the client's in-memory counter. This led to underreporting. The Private installs affected were running agent v2025.11 which had a stricter TTL than the hosted ingestion tier.

Immediate mitigations applied: 1) Deployed a short-term patch to ingestion nodes that disables expiration-based dropping and instead routes potentially-stale envelopes to a fallback persistent queue (hotfix runtime-1.21.1) to avoid drops. 2) Updated SDKs to include a monotonic request-id and server-ack backoff so client counters are not decremented until server ack is received (temporary client-side guard). 3) Opened billing adjustments for impacted customers pending full reconciliation.

Investigation notes and evidence: - Grafana dashboard: "metering.pipeline.drop_rate" spiked to 4.8% during the window (https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/metering-overview). - Support tickets: SUP-4321, SUP-4330, SUP-4337. - Repro: Simulated 50k sub-100ms short-response requests with artificial ingestion delays >60s; reproduced 3.9% undercount. - Private agent logs (customer CUST-889) show TTL eviction entries with code EXPIRE_30S. - GitHub PR with hotfix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingestion/pull/2748

Root cause decision: The immediate root cause is a defensive memory-pressure eviction policy combined with a client-side counter decrement before durable acknowledgement. Fix path requires both server-side persistence fallback and client-side counter safety.

Next steps (short term, within cycle): - Complete rollout of runtime-1.21.1 to all ingestion nodes (owner: Liam Chen, ETA: 2026-03-14). - Backfill dropped envelopes for the 2026-03-07 -> 2026-03-08 window by replaying from persistent queue snapshot and reconciling token deltas (owner: Data Eng, ETA: 2026-03-18). - Ship SDK update v2.7.3 with ack-based counter semantics and telemetry (owner: SDK team, ETA: 2026-03-16). - Issue invoice adjustments and communicate post-mortem to affected customers (owner: Customer Success, ETA: 2026-03-17).

Longer-term actions (post-cycle): - Replace in-memory TTL eviction with a tiered eviction policy that samples and persists borderline envelopes to cheap object storage rather than dropping. - Add an end-to-end metering invariant test to the CI harness that injects variable ingestion latency and asserts no undercount >0.1%. - Rework SDK-server handshake to ensure idempotent counters and proof-of-consumption receipts.

Notes for PM/Finance: We recommend issuing provisional credits for the impacted billing period while we finish the reconciliation. Estimated credit exposure < $12k across customers. Will provide a final reconciliation report after backfill completes.
